concepts.electron.title: Electron
concepts.electron.summary: A straight line with the arrow pointing forward in time.
concepts.electron.body: An elementary particle with charge −1, responsible for chemistry and electricity. It is a fermion: two identical electrons cannot occupy the same state.
concepts.photon.title: Photon
concepts.photon.summary: A wavy line. The particle of light.
concepts.photon.body: The quantum of the electromagnetic field. It has no mass and no charge. It carries the electromagnetic force between charged particles.
concepts.time.title: Time convention
concepts.time.summary: Time runs from left to right.
concepts.time.body: On the left we draw the initial state (what comes in) and on the right the final state (what goes out). Other books use the vertical axis: it's just a convention.
concepts.initial-final.title: Initial and final state
concepts.initial-final.summary: What comes in and what goes out.
concepts.initial-final.body: External lines represent the real particles that are prepared and detected. Everything else happens in between.
concepts.positron.title: Positron
concepts.positron.summary: A straight line with the arrow pointing backward in time.
concepts.positron.body: The electron's antiparticle: same mass and charge +1. Dirac predicted it in 1928 and Anderson discovered it in 1932.
concepts.annihilation.title: Annihilation
concepts.annihilation.summary: Matter and antimatter turn into light.
concepts.annihilation.body: An electron and a positron disappear and produce two photons. It's the principle behind PET scans in medicine.
concepts.not-trajectory.title: Not a trajectory
concepts.not-trajectory.summary: A diagram is a piece of a calculation, not a photo.
concepts.not-trajectory.body: Feynman diagrams represent contributions to a probability amplitude. The positions and angles in the drawing have no physical meaning.
concepts.vertex.title: QED vertex
concepts.vertex.summary: Three lines: an arrow in, an arrow out and a photon.
concepts.vertex.body: The only fundamental interaction of quantum electrodynamics. Each vertex contributes a factor of the charge e.
concepts.charge.title: Charge conservation
concepts.charge.body: At every vertex, one arrow comes in and another goes out. The total charge before and after any process is the same.
concepts.qed-rule.title: Forbidden vertices
concepts.qed-rule.summary: No four lines and no two photons at a vertex.
concepts.qed-rule.body: QED has only one fundamental vertex. More complex processes are built by chaining three-line vertices.
concepts.admissible.title: Allowed ≠ possible
concepts.admissible.summary: A correct vertex is not a possible process on its own.
concepts.admissible.body: Processes with three real free particles violate conservation of energy and momentum. A vertex is a piece of a bigger diagram.
concepts.crossing.title: Crossing symmetry
concepts.crossing.summary: A rotated vertex tells another story.
concepts.crossing.body: Emission, absorption, annihilation and pair creation are the same vertex oriented in different ways with respect to time.
concepts.internal-external.title: Internal and external lines
concepts.internal-external.body: An external line touches an edge of the diagram. An internal one joins two vertices and represents a virtual particle.
concepts.moller.title: Møller scattering
concepts.moller.summary: Two electrons repel each other by exchanging a photon.
concepts.moller.body: It has two tree-level diagrams, t and u, which are subtracted because electrons are identical fermions.
concepts.virtual.title: Virtual photon
concepts.virtual.body: An internal photon that carries momentum between two vertices. It never reaches a detector and doesn't satisfy the energy–momentum relation of a free photon.
concepts.bhabha.title: Bhabha scattering
concepts.bhabha.body: It has two contributions: scattering (t channel) and annihilation (s channel). It's used to measure the luminosity of colliders.
concepts.virtual-electron.title: Virtual electron
concepts.virtual-electron.body: It appears in annihilation and in Compton scattering. Its propagator is i(q̸ + m)/(q² − m²).
concepts.tree-level.title: Tree level
concepts.tree-level.body: They are the simplest (lowest-order) contributions to a process. Loops are smaller corrections, suppressed by factors of α ≈ 1/137.
concepts.compton.title: Compton scattering
concepts.compton.body: Its discovery in 1923 showed that light carries momentum like a particle. It has contributions from the s and u channels.
concepts.topology.title: Topology
concepts.topology.summary: What matters is what connects to what, not how it's drawn.
concepts.topology.body: Two drawings with the same connections are the same diagram. Topologically different diagrams are different contributions.
concepts.identical.title: Identical particles
concepts.identical.summary: If you can't tell them apart, every story counts.
concepts.identical.body: With two identical final electrons you must include both the direct and the crossed diagram.
concepts.channels.title: s, t and u channels
concepts.channels.summary: The three ways to pair up four particles.
concepts.channels.body: s: the two initial particles share a vertex. t: each initial particle with “its” final one. u: crossed. The charge rules decide which ones exist.
concepts.contributions.title: Counting diagrams
concepts.contributions.summary: Every diagram, not one more, not one less.
concepts.contributions.body: The first step of a calculation is to list every topologically distinct contribution at the desired order.
concepts.pair-production.title: Pair production
concepts.pair-production.body: Two photons with enough energy can create an electron and a positron (the Breit–Wheeler process).
concepts.order.title: Perturbative order
concepts.order.summary: Each vertex contributes a factor e.
concepts.order.body: With n vertices, the amplitude goes as eⁿ. Since α ≈ 1/137 is small, diagrams with more vertices contribute less and less.
concepts.bremsstrahlung.title: Bremsstrahlung
concepts.bremsstrahlung.body: German for “braking radiation”. It's a three-vertex process, suppressed by a factor of α compared with scattering without a photon. It's how fast electrons lose energy in matter and how X-ray tubes work.
concepts.positronium.title: Positronium
concepts.positronium.summary: An atom of matter and antimatter.
concepts.positronium.body: A bound electron and positron. With parallel spins (ortho-positronium) it can only decay into three photons and lives about 142 ns; with opposite spins (para-positronium), into two, and it lives about 0.12 ns.
concepts.bosons.title: Identical bosons
concepts.bosons.summary: Swapping them doesn't change the sign.
concepts.bosons.body: The amplitudes of identical photons add with the same sign (symmetric). Those of identical fermions, with alternating sign (antisymmetric). That's where lasers and the exclusion principle come from.
concepts.loop.title: Loop
concepts.loop.summary: A closed circuit of internal lines.
concepts.loop.body: Each loop leaves a free momentum that has to be integrated over. Loops are quantum corrections suppressed by a factor of α, and studying them led to renormalization.
concepts.vacuum-polarization.title: Vacuum polarization
concepts.vacuum-polarization.body: Virtual electron–positron pairs make the effective charge grow at short distances: α goes from ≈ 1/137 to ≈ 1/128 at the energy of the Z boson.
concepts.g-2.title: Anomalous magnetic moment
concepts.g-2.body: The vertex loop corrects the electron's magnet by 0.116%. It's the most precise prediction in science: theory and experiment agree to more than 10 digits.
concepts.light-by-light.title: Light on light
concepts.light-by-light.body: Impossible in classical physics. In QED it happens through a loop of virtual electrons (6 box diagrams). ATLAS observed it in 2017.
concepts.furry.title: Furry's theorem
concepts.furry.summary: Loops with an odd number of photons cancel out.
concepts.furry.body: The two orientations of an electron loop cancel when it carries an odd number of photons. It's a consequence of charge-conjugation symmetry.
concepts.interference.title: Interference
concepts.interference.body: Diagrams are combined before squaring. For identical fermions, the exchange contributes a minus sign.
